steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Judges are appointed by the King on the advice of the Prime Minister and Lord Chancellor — they must be independent | Key Fact: The principle of judicial independence means judges are free from political pressure and cannot be removed easily | Key Fact: Judges are appointed through the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC) based on merit through open competition | Key Fact: Magistrates are unpaid volunteers — around 12,000 sit in England and Wales, hearing 95% of criminal cases
